theory.intro: The projectile model gives $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $g$ positive and up positive. Integrating once and using the initial velocity gives $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$. Integrating again and using the initial position gives $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
facts: Each integration introduces a **constant of integration** in each component, found from the initial conditions.
The horizontal acceleration is zero, so $\dot{x}=V\cos\alpha$ stays the same for the whole flight.
The vertical velocity is $\dot{y}=-gt+V\sin\alpha$, dropping by $g$ every second.
Integrating again from the origin gives $x=Vt\cos\alpha$ and $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}+Vt\sin\alpha$.

For a launch from height $h$, placing the origin at ground level directly below launch gives $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=h\underset{\sim}{j}$, which adds $h$ to $y$. The booklet recommends placing the origin at the launch point instead, so $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$ and ground level is $y=-h$.
You are expected to derive the six equations unless they are given in the question, with marks allocated for the derivation.
steps: Write the acceleration in vector form
Use the initial velocity to find the constants
Use the initial position to find the constants

workedExamples.question_text: A ball is projected from the origin at $28\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$. By integrating, derive the six equations of motion and write the velocity and position in vector form.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Take right and up as positive. The initial velocity components are
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}(0)&=28\cos30^{\circ}=14\sqrt{3}\\\dot{y}(0)&=28\sin30^{\circ}=14.\end{align*}$

The acceleration components are $\ddot{x}=0$ and $\ddot{y}=-10$.

Integrate the horizontal acceleration:
$\begin{align*}\dot{x}&=\int0\,dt=C_{1}\\\dot{x}(0)&=C_{1}=14\sqrt{3}\\\dot{x}(t)&=14\sqrt{3}.\end{align*}$

Integrate the vertical acceleration:
$\begin{align*}\dot{y}&=\int-10\,dt=-10t+C_{2}\\14&=-10(0)+C_{2}\\C_{2}&=14\\\dot{y}(t)&=14-10t.\end{align*}$

Integrate again and use $x(0)=y(0)=0$:
$\begin{align*}x&=\int14\sqrt{3}\,dt=14\sqrt{3}t+C_{3}\\0&=14\sqrt{3}(0)+C_{3}\\C_{3}&=0\\x(t)&=14\sqrt{3}t.\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}y&=\int(14-10t)\,dt=14t-5t^{2}+C_{4}\\0&=14(0)-5(0)^{2}+C_{4}\\C_{4}&=0\\y(t)&=14t-5t^{2}.\end{align*}$

The six equations are
$\begin{align*}\ddot{x}&=0,&\ddot{y}&=-10,\\\dot{x}&=14\sqrt{3},&\dot{y}&=14-10t,\\x&=14\sqrt{3}t,&y&=14t-5t^{2}.\end{align*}$

In vector form,
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{a}(t)&=-10\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{v}(t)&=14\sqrt{3}\underset{\sim}{i}+(14-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}\\\underset{\sim}{r}(t)&=14\sqrt{3}t\underset{\sim}{i}+(14t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}.\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A stone is projected at $18\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. Take right and up as positive and $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^{2}$. By integrating the acceleration, find its velocity vector at time $t$.
A projectile starts at the origin with velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=13\underset{\sim}{i}+(16-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second. Find its position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Integrate each component:
$\begin{align*}x&=\int13\,dt=13t+C_{1}\\y&=\int(16-10t)\,dt=16t-5t^{2}+C_{2}.\end{align*}$

The projectile starts at the origin, so $x(0)=0$ and $y(0)=0$:
$\begin{align*}0&=13(0)+C_{1}\\C_{1}&=0\\0&=16(0)-5(0)^{2}+C_{2}\\C_{2}&=0.\end{align*}$

Hence,
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=13t\underset{\sim}{i}+(16t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}\text{ m}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A ball is thrown from a platform $18\text{ m}$ above the ground at $45\text{ m/s}$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal, where $\tan\theta=\dfrac{4}{3}$. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and the origin at ground level directly below launch. By integrating, find its velocity and position vectors.

A projectile has position vector $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=15t\underset{\sim}{i}+(20t-4.9t^{2}+8)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, with $y$ measured from the ground. Find its launch speed and angle above the horizontal, giving the angle to $1$ decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Differentiate the position vector:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=15\underset{\sim}{i}+(20-9.8t)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

At launch,
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=15\underset{\sim}{i}+20\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Use the initial components to find the speed:
$\begin{align*}V&=\sqrt{15^{2}+20^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{625}\\&=25\text{ m/s}.\end{align*}$

Both components are positive, so the direction is above the horizontal:
$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{20}{15}\right)\\&\approx53.1^{\circ}.\end{align*}$

The launch velocity is $25\text{ m/s}$ at $53.1^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.

workedExamples.question_text: A projectile starts at the origin with speed $U$ at angle $\beta$ above the horizontal. Its acceleration is $\underset{\sim}{a}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$, where $g>0$. Integrate twice and use the initial conditions to derive its velocity and position vectors.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Integrating the acceleration gives
$\underset{\sim}{v}=C_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+(-gt+C_{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Use the initial velocity:
$\begin{align*}\underset{\sim}{v}(0)&=U\cos\beta\,\underset{\sim}{i}+U\sin\beta\,\underset{\sim}{j}\\C_{1}&=U\cos\beta\\C_{2}&=U\sin\beta.\end{align*}$

Therefore,
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=U\cos\beta\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(U\sin\beta-gt)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

Integrating again gives
$\underset{\sim}{r}=(Ut\cos\beta+C_{3})\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Ut\sin\beta-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}+C_{4}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

The launch point is the origin, so $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$. Thus $C_{3}=0$ and $C_{4}=0$, giving
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=Ut\cos\beta\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Ut\sin\beta-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

foundation.question_text:
A ball is thrown from the origin at $24\text{ m/s}$ at $60^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
By integrating, find $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ in exact form.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Write the acceleration in vector form**
$\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=0\underset{\sim}{i}-10\underset{\sim}{j}$
2. **Integrate to find the velocity**
$\underset{\sim}{v}=C_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+(-10t+C_{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$
3. **Use the initial velocity to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=24\cos 60^{\circ}\,\underset{\sim}{i}+24\sin 60^{\circ}\,\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=12\underset{\sim}{i}+12\sqrt{3}\underset{\sim}{j}$
$C_{1}=12$ and $C_{2}=12\sqrt{3}$
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=12\underset{\sim}{i}+(12\sqrt{3}-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$

foundation.question_text:

Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
foundation.solution_text:
4. **Integrate to find the position**
$\underset{\sim}{r}=(9t+C_{3})\underset{\sim}{i}+(20t-5t^{2}+C_{4})\underset{\sim}{j}$
5. **Use the initial position to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$
$C_{3}=0$ and $C_{4}=0$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=9t\underset{\sim}{i}+(20t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$

mastery.question_text:
A projectile is launched from the origin with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal, with $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$.
By integrating twice, show that $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=Vt\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
mastery.solution_text:
2. **Integrate to find the velocity**
$\underset{\sim}{v}=C_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+(-gt+C_{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$
3. **Use the initial velocity to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=V\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+V\sin\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{j}$
$C_{1}=V\cos\alpha$ and $C_{2}=V\sin\alpha$
$\underset{\sim}{v}=V\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(V\sin\alpha-gt)\underset{\sim}{j}$
4. **Integrate to find the position**
$\underset{\sim}{r}=(Vt\cos\alpha+C_{3})\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}+C_{4}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$
5. **Use the initial position to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$, so $C_{3}=0$ and $C_{4}=0$
$\underset{\sim}{r}=Vt\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$

mastery.question_text:
A projectile launched from a tower has $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=18t\underset{\sim}{i}+(24t-5t^{2}+30)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, with $y$ measured from the ground.
Find the launch speed and angle to 1 d.p.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=18\underset{\sim}{i}+(24-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=18\underset{\sim}{i}+24\underset{\sim}{j}$
$V=\sqrt{18^{2}+24^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{900}$
$=30$
$\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{24}{18}\right)$
$\approx 53.1^{\circ}$
The launch was at $30.0\text{ m/s}$, $53.1^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
